inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 63.400m outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) less 0.479m repurchased 1-27 Oct 2026 (10-Q subsequent-event note; the $86.7m paid is deducted in equity_bridge) plus 1.669m treasury-method dilution from SSARs/RSUs/PSUs (Q3 diluted 65.504m less basic 63.835m). Held FLAT: SBC and the net-share-settlement tax are expensed in the flows. DaVita in fact retires far more than it grants (diluted count 93.2m FY2023 -> 65.5m Q3-2026), funded by FCF plus debt; that shrinkage is treated as value-neutral, not modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3-2026: cash-flow-statement stock-based compensation expense 121.8 (FY2025 140.0 - 9M-2025 101.6 + 9M-2026 83.4) PLUS payment of tax withholdings on net share settlements 70.5 (FY2025 35.3 - 9M-2025 33.8 + 9M-2026 69.0), financing activities. DaVita publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule. The withholding line is lumpy (FY2024 134.0, FY2025 35.3).
inputs.buyback_note: TTM treasury purchases: 9M-2026 870.2 (450.9 open market + 419.3 from Berkshire under the April-2024 agreement that holds Berkshire at 45%) plus Q4-2025 274.5. Actual financing outflow, not authorisation. Repurchaser: the flat count is more than funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered equity beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (TTM debt expense 594 on ~10.5bn average debt; SOFR+1.50-1.75% term loans, 3.75-6.875% notes) -> ~4.1% after tax. Market weights ~52% equity / 48% net debt give ~7.1%; rounded UP to 8.0% because the capital structure sits at the top of the 3.0-3.5x leverage target with the 2030-31 maturity wall inside the horizon. Same WACC in all three scenarios: regulatory and payor-mix risk is charged in the flows and the weights, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), by construction of US GAAP: operating-lease rent (ASC 842) is already inside patient care costs and G&A, so adjusted EBITDA is post-rent and the 2,623 of operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance lease obligations (151.6) are inside total_debt and their amortisation inside D&A. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows. ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA NET of the noncontrolling partners' share (TTM ~335: distributions to NCI 335.4; NCI income 298.6 reported, ~333 before the 34 NCI share of the China impairment). The JV partnerships are pass-through entities, so the NCI share is a pre-tax deduction and cash_tax_rate_path is the rate attributable to DaVita Inc. Neither the 1,484 of puttable NCI (fair value, temporary equity) nor the 233 of other NCI is deducted in the bridge - that would charge it twice. Purchases of NCI (70.6 in 9M-2026) are treated as discretionary reinvestment.
inputs.net_debt_note: Debt 10,769.1 = 10,832.2 principal less 63.1 discount/financing costs (Term Loan A-2 1,962.5; Term Loan B-2 2,352.0; revolver 80.0; senior notes 6,250.0; other notes 36.2; finance leases 151.6). Cash 566.3 = cash and equivalents 495.6 + short-term investments 70.7; restricted cash 83.6 excluded.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US dialysis services). Routed as an operating company despite negative book equity (-591): the deficit is the residue of debt-funded buybacks, not operating losses, so equity/book-value methods are meaningless and the leverage is handled where it belongs - full net debt in the bridge, unlevered flows, and a bear case that prices the regulatory/refinancing risk. Adaptations applied: NCI (flows-only), leases (rent already in EBITDA), non-operating asset (Elara at cost). FY0 is the TTM to 30 Sep 2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet stops; Y1 is therefore approximately FY2027 and FY2026 guidance (adjusted OI 2,175-2,250, FCF 1,000-1,250) is the cross-check on FY0, not a forecast year: TTM adjusted OI is 2,208 (FY2025 2,094 - 9M-2025 1,508 + 9M-2026 1,622). FY0 adjusted EBITDA pre-SBC = 2,208 + D&A 697.5 + SBC 121.8 = 3,027 (21.4% of revenue); net of NCI 335 = 2,692 (19.0%). last_fcf (787.7) is the LEVERED company-definition FCF (OCF less NCI distributions less maintenance and development capex plus NCI contributions and sale-leaseback proceeds; TTM 980 = FY2025 1,024 - 9M-2025 716 + 9M-2026 672) less SBC incl. withholding taxes; the projections are UNLEVERED (before ~445 after-tax interest), which is why Y1 FCF is ~1.45bn. Interest income is not stripped: the company is in net debt. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Terminal value binds on the cap multiple, not Gordon, in base and bear. Sanity multiples: at the current price EV (equity 11.3bn + net debt 10.2bn) is ~7.1x TTM adjusted EBITDA pre-NCI and ~15x Y1 unlevered owner FCF.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is undefined: shareholders' equity went from +1,567 (FY2020) to -651 (FY2025) through debt-funded buybacks, so the house primary (book-value CAGR) cannot be used. EPS growth (9-19%) runs far ahead of revenue (3-5%) because the diluted count fell from 122.6m to 75.9m over the same five years; revenue is the only undistorted series.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025. FCF series is OCF less capex less SBC less equity-award withholding taxes (FY2025 1,135; FY2022 810; FY2020 ~1,211 with FY2020 withholding taxes not disclosed in the extracted filings and taken as ~2), i.e. before NCI distributions. Owner FCF has gone nowhere in five years while reported EPS rose 56%: the per-share growth is financial engineering on a flat cash base.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA before SBC and NET of the NCI partners' share, as % of revenue. FY0 actual 19.0%.
base.sbc_pct_note: FY0 actual 1.36% incl. withholding taxes; held flat - a mature issuer with no stated plan to cut grants.
base.da_pct_note: FY0 4.9% and falling as assets become fully depreciated (10-Q MD&A); converges toward capex.
base.capex_pct_note: FY0 4.07% (maintenance ~2.9% + development ~1.2%, before ~0.1-0.2% sale-leaseback proceeds). Acquisition spend (42 in 9M-2026, 118 in 9M-2025) is excluded and so is acquired growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Effective rate attributable to DaVita Inc. 26.5% for 9M-2026 (29.1% FY2025 incl. a tax-claim write-down, 22.9% FY2024). Cash taxes ran below the provision in FY2025 (177 paid) on deferred-tax timing; not perpetuated.
base.wc_capture_note: Negative: receivables (2.5bn, ~64 days) grow with revenue; this is a provider billing payors in arrears, not a prepaid model.

scenario_narratives.base: The duopoly bends but holds. US treatment volume stays roughly flat (normalised non-acquired growth was -0.8% in FY2025) and revenue grows 3-3.5% on revenue per treatment, Integrated Kidney Care shared savings and international centres, fading to 2.5%. Patient-care cost per treatment (+2.4% YoY in Q3-2026), supplies and professional liability keep pace with or slightly outrun Medicare's market-basket update, and the loss of enhanced ACA premium credits trims commercial mix at the edge, so the margin net of JV partners drifts from 19.0% to 18.8% rather than expanding. The October-2026 HHS Kidney Care National Plan produces rule-making on home dialysis and transplant access but no direct cut to commercial pricing. Capital intensity stays near 4% of revenue. Exit at 14x unlevered owner FCF, below Gordon, because a buyer of a regulated, levered provider under explicit federal scrutiny will not pay a compounder multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: The HHS plan proves to be mostly prevention and transplant policy with little bite on in-centre economics; mortality normalises and treatment volume returns to the 1-2% growth the ESKD population supports (~3.3% CAGR 2012-2022), IKC keeps beating (FY2026 IKC adjusted OI guidance raised to at least 65) and scales into the 2027 LEAD model, and international growth continues. Revenue grows 4-4.5% and operating leverage plus IKC profit lift the net-of-NCI margin from 19.0% to 20.0% over five years. Requires volume recovery, benign regulation and cost discipline together.
scenario_narratives.bear: Federal policy does what it says: measures to break the DaVita/Fresenius 74% share erode commercial rates or steer commercially insured patients away, and commercial mix (27-33% of US dialysis revenue, nearly all of the profit) shrinks as ACA subsidies lapse. Because the profit pool is concentrated in that slice, revenue only slows to 1-2% but the net-of-NCI margin falls 350bp to 15.5% over five years while labour, supply and liability costs keep rising. With ~10.2bn of net debt and 2030-2031 maturities to refinance, the equity absorbs the whole decline; exit at 11x. Securities-litigation and Anti-Kickback/Stark exposure are not separately costed.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: profit depends on a single regulator's rate-setting and on a commercial-mix slice that the October-2026 HHS plan explicitly targets, and leverage near 3.5x turns any margin loss into a multiple of itself at the equity line. Base 50%: the duopoly's licensing, physician-JV and scale barriers have survived two decades of policy pressure and FY2026 guidance was nudged up after the plan was announced. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs volume recovery, benign regulation and cost control to arrive together, and five years of flat owner FCF give no evidence of it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DaVita is a slow-growing, highly cash-generative regulated service business whose per-share record has been manufactured by leverage and buybacks rather than by growth in owner cash flow. It is valued on unlevered owner FCF after the JV partners' share, SBC and net-settlement taxes, with the full 10.2bn of net debt deducted. Equity is the thin residual of a large enterprise value, so small changes in margin, exit multiple or WACC move the per-share value by tens of dollars; the scenario spread, not the point estimate, is the finding.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: net debt is ~47% of enterprise value, so a 10% change in EV moves equity value by roughly 20%; the bear case loses well over half the base value on a 350bp margin decline.
Regulatory: the October-2026 HHS Kidney Care National Plan targets market concentration; its effect on commercial rates and mix is unknowable today and is the main bear axis.
Commercial mix: ~11% of patients generate nearly all profit; ACA premium-credit expiry and employment trends act directly on it.
Terminal value binds on the cap multiple (14x base, 11x bear), a judgment; each turn of exit multiple is worth roughly 13-14 per share in the base case.
Refinancing: ~9.5bn of term loans and notes mature 2030-2033, inside the explicit horizon; the 8.0% WACC assumes they roll at similar spreads.
NCI is charged through the flows at ~2.4% of revenue; puttable NCI of 1,484 at fair value is a contingent cash call not deducted separately.
SBC basis sums expense and withholding taxes (no combined company figure); if that double-counts, value is understated by up to roughly 15-20 per share.
